name: ESPN / ABC
parent: The Walt Disney Company (ESPN is about 80% Disney / 20% Hearst; the NFL was to take a 10% stake as part of the 2025 NFL Network deal)
streaming: ESPN app DTC ('ESPN Unlimited' flagship, $29.99/mo, launched Aug. 21, 2025)
currentCollegeProperties: ncaa (40 championships incl. women's basketball, through 2031-32)
SEC/ACC/Big 12 championship games (end after the 2026 season)
Big 12 Now / SEC Network+ / ACCNX streaming
appetite: Largest college buyer by volume; owns the CFP and two conference networks. Strategy is depth (SEC/ACC/Big 12 plus G6 inventory for ESPN2/ESPNU and streaming) rather than paying top dollar for every P4 window. Walked away from the Big Ten in 2022 rather than pay about $380M a year for a secondary package. Said 'no one is expecting a financial windfall' from the 24-team playoff, then still paid about $345M a year more for it. Will defend its CFP and SEC holdings at almost any price.

name: FOX Sports
currentCollegeProperties: big-ten (lead partner, Big Noon Saturday, through 2029-30; BTN majority owner)
mountain-west (12 games plus championship game, through 2031-32)
Big Ten Championship Game (2023, 2025, 2026 via buyback; 2027 and 2029 removed by the 24-team CFP)

keyExecs.name: Michael Mulvihill
keyExecs.title: President, Insights & Analytics, FOX Sports (lead college-rights strategist)

appetite: A broadcast-first, 'no cable bundle needed' strategy built around Big Noon Saturday. Concentrates on the Big Ten (through BTN equity and licensing control) and the Big 12. Willing to buy back premium games (paid $45-55M for NBC's 2026 Big Ten title game) and to block rivals' sublicensing to streamers. Less interested in G6 except the MW.

name: CBS Sports
currentCollegeProperties: ncaa men's basketball tournament (with TNT, through 2032)
Big Ten Championship Game 2028 (removed by the 24-team CFP)
appetite: Gave up the SEC in 2020 rather than pay about 5.5x, but bought the Big Ten 3:30 window in 2022. Now the main buyer of 'second-tier' broadcast windows (Pac-12, MW) and a CBSSN aggregator of G6 inventory. Under Ellison, Paramount is spending aggressively on sports (UFC) and pursued Warner Bros. Discovery, which would combine CBS and TNT, partners on the NCAA tournament, and remove a bidder.

recentBids.note: Declined to match ESPN's about $300M a year

note: Dan Weinberg's and George Cheeks' titles are from prior knowledge. Reported in Feb. 2026: Paramount agreed to acquire WBD after Netflix declined to raise its bid; closing and regulatory status unverified.

name: NBC Sports
currentCollegeProperties: big-ten ('Big Ten Saturday Night' primetime plus Peacock exclusives, through 2029-30)
appetite: Uses college primetime and Notre Dame to drive Peacock sign-ups. Its NBA deal (from 2025-26) strains budget and primetime capacity, as shown by the April 2026 sale of its 2026 Big Ten title game to FOX. Lost cable outlets (USA, Golf) in the Versant spin-off, so it relies more on NBC broadcast plus Peacock.
note: Pete Bevacqua, the former NBC Sports chairman, is now Notre Dame's AD. Exec titles from prior knowledge.

name: Versant (USA Network / USA Sports)
parent: Versant Media Group (spun off from Comcast/NBCUniversal; completed about Jan. 2026)
currentCollegeProperties: pac-12 (22 football games a year, through 2030-31)
appetite: A new standalone cable company that needs live sports to support carriage fees. Proven buyer of mid-tier college football (the Pac-12) at modest prices. Aliases: 'usa', 'usa-network'. Other agents may file USA Network deals under 'nbc'.
note: Spin-off timing and exec from prior knowledge.

name: TNT Sports
parent: Warner Bros. Discovery (planned 'Discovery Global' networks spin; Paramount Skydance reportedly agreed in early 2026 to acquire WBD, pending)
currentCollegeProperties: ncaa men's basketball tournament (with CBS, through 2032)
cfp (ESPN sublicense: first-round and some quarterfinal games)
appetite: Lost the NBA after 2024-25, so it is hungry for premium live events and has rebuilt with college (CFP sublicense, Big East), NASCAR, the French Open and others. Prefers sublicenses from ESPN over carrying full conference packages. Its future depends on who ends up owning WBD.
note: WBD/Netflix/Paramount sequence (Netflix deal Dec. 2025, Paramount hostile bid, then a reported Paramount agreement in Feb. 2026) from prior knowledge; verify the current status.

name: The CW
currentCollegeProperties: pac-12 (13 football, 35 men's basketball, 15 women's basketball games a year, through 2030-31)
mountain-west (13 football games a year, through 2030-31)
acc (sublicensed football and basketball from ESPN)
appetite: Low-cost aggregator of college football for its Saturday schedule (broadcast reach about 100% of U.S. TV homes). Pays modest fees and lets conferences self-produce (Pac-12 Enterprises), which makes it the natural floor bidder for G6 and rebuilt leagues.

name: Amazon Prime Video

keyExecs.name: Jay Marine
keyExecs.title: VP & Global Head, Prime Video Sports

keyExecs.name: Mike Hopkins
keyExecs.title: SVP, Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios

appetite: Big pro-sports buyer: NFL Thursday Night Football plus a Black Friday NFL game since 2023, the NBA from 2025-26, NASCAR, WNBA. Has bid on college packages (the Big Ten in 2022, early Pac-12 talks in 2022-23) without winning. Wants national, exclusive, 'tentpole' inventory (Black Friday-style events) rather than full conference slates. The most credible streaming disruptor for a game-model bidding war.

recentBids.note: Bid for a package; FOX/CBS/NBC chosen
Dropped out of the Kliavkoff process

note: No major college rights as of mid-2026 (from prior knowledge).

name: Netflix
appetite: Buys 'events', not seasons: NFL Christmas games (2024 onward, about 24M viewers each in 2024), WWE Raw (10 years, about $5B), boxing, MLB event packages from 2026, and the 2027/2031 Women's World Cups in the U.S. Has said it is not interested in full regular-season packages, so college interest is likely limited to one-off neutral-site or bowl-style events.
note: From prior knowledge. Netflix's bid for Warner Bros. (Dec. 2025) was reportedly topped by Paramount in early 2026.

name: Apple TV
appetite: Global, all-in, subscription-led deals: MLS Season Pass (10 years, about $2.5B from 2023; folded into the base Apple TV subscription from 2026 and reportedly ending early), and U.S. Formula 1 rights from 2026. Its 2023 Pac-12 offer was subscriber-contingent with little linear TV, and presidents rejected it. Model as a high-variance bidder that pays on subscriptions, not guarantees.

name: YouTube / YouTube TV
appetite: Main role in college is as a distributor: carriage fights with Disney (ESPN/SEC Network/ACCN blackout Oct. 30 to Nov. 14, 2025) and other programmers. Rights buying so far is NFL-focused (Sunday Ticket about $2B a year; a free 2025 NFL Brazil game). A potential free-to-view bidder for one-off college events.

name: Kiswe
streaming: White-label DTC platforms (Mountain West subscription service from July 2026)
appetite: Technology/operating partner for conference-owned DTC services, paid through subscription revenue share rather than rights fees.

name: Scripps Sports (ION)
appetite: Over-the-air buyer of women's and regional sports (WNBA, NWSL, local NHL). A plausible low-cost bidder for G6 or FCS football and women's basketball packages; no major college conference package was confirmed.
note: College holdings not verified this session.

appetite: Subscription streamer of niche and FCS-level college sports; pays small fees.
